events.who: 辛西娅（辛西娅·布尔洛斯，Cynthia）
events.did: 在走廊里来回踱步，攒了十年的怒气：丈夫未经她同意就辞退了她的贴身女仆
events.verbatim: Cynthia was well and truly vexed. She strode along the hallway… ‘The very nerve of that man! To sack my maid without even bothering to consult me,’ Cynthia muttered, building up steam for the tirade that had been brewing for ten years. Ten years of keeping her mouth shut. Ten years of being the dutiful wife her husband required.

events.did: 在心里宣告不再继续过这种生活，并且决定这次要当面质问丈夫
events.verbatim: No more. I will not continue to live this way. … It was time her husband explained himself. And not just about the maid.

events.who: 辛西娅（对这段婚姻的判断）
events.did: 认定丈夫掌管家务决定是自己仅剩的那一点自主；情妇之事她能忍，其余（他消失数日至数周、回来一身劣酒与廉价香水味、与律师密谈后大发雷霆）不可忍受，她因此躲回自己那侧房间
events.verbatim: Hubert taking control of household decisions, the one domain where she held a smidge of autonomy, was beyond the pale. … Days – sometimes weeks – where he disappeared, only to return reeking of stale gin and cheap perfume. … Cynthia kept to her wing of their Mayfair home

events.did: 自称「完美的社交婚姻」，借出席社交活动证明一切安好
events.verbatim: She had done her best to paint a smile on her lips. She put on her social armour right along with her shift, corset, stays, and fashionable gowns. Swanning about at all the desirable events with the beau monde, she strove to prove nothing was amiss. All was well in her perfect society marriage.

events.who: 女管家希金斯太太（Mrs Higgins，housekeeper）／被辞退的女仆 Lily
events.did: 早上辛西娅叫人，来的是女管家；女管家满脸通红、垂着眼告知 Lily 已被辞退
events.verbatim: But something changed when she called for her maid that morning, only to have Mrs Higgins, the housekeeper, arrive instead. With crimson cheeks and a lowered gaze, she told Cynthia Lily had been dismissed.

events.did: 推开书房门，看见丈夫面朝下趴在奥比松地毯上，血积成一汪深红
events.verbatim: Her righteous anger felt glorious… as she pushed open the door to his study. … He was sprawled face down on the thick Aubusson rug. Blood pooled around him like a large crimson lake.

events.did: 晴空无云时响了一声雷（此时是伦敦仲夏），随后窗外暴雨、黑云蔽日
events.verbatim: Something broke in Cynthia as lightning cracked in the cloudless blue sky. Which was odd, given that it was mid-summer in London and hardly a stormy season. … A summer storm raged outside the window. Thunder boomed, loud enough to rattle the glass. Black clouds covered the bright sun

events.who: 管家、两名男仆、希金斯太太、警员
events.did: 管家一看见 Lord Hubert Burrows 就当场呕吐在门边的花盆里；一名男仆面如白纸瘫倒；希金斯太太把哭闹的女仆赶出去并端来热茶，硬塞进辛西娅发抖的手里
events.verbatim: The butler hurried into the room, took one look at Lord Hubert Burrows, and swiftly tossed up his accounts in the potted palm by the door. … Mrs Higgins, who ushered the hysterical maids out and came back with a tray of tea, forcing the hot cup into Cynthia’s shaking hand.

events.did: 出现在她面前，黑发凌乱、绿眼里有近乎恐惧的神色，说不出话来
events.verbatim: Her brother stood in front of her, his black hair askew, his green eyes flashing with something akin to fear. He seemed at a loss for words, something he had never been before. … ‘Thomas. What are you doing here?’

events.who: 苏格兰场警司 Lachlan MacDougal（辛西娅哥哥的朋友）
events.did: 手里端着一杯茶出现；她从没见过警司喝茶
events.verbatim: Another man stepped into her line of vision. His mess of curly hair was in direct contrast to the crisp white cravat, starched collar and smart jacket of Superintendent Lachlan MacDougal. He held a cup of tea in his hands. Which was very strange indeed. She had never seen the superintendent drink tea.

events.did: 哥哥是 MacDougal 的挚友，「十多年前」曾把他扛过战场送回家治疗；MacDougal 只来吃过一次饭
events.verbatim: Her brother’s best friend – the man who had carried poor Thomas across battlefields littered with dead men so that he could be patched up and sent home to her over a decade ago – had only come to dinner once.

events.did: 五个月前结识 Clio Blair；Clio 当时在跟她哥哥查一桩案子，两人相恋并已 recently married，计划婚后旅行但要等到秋天
events.verbatim: She met Clio Blair five months prior, when the young lady had been investigating a case with Cynthia’s brother. Predictably, Thomas and Clio fell in love and were recently married. They were planning a wedding tour, but mercifully, Clio wanted to wait until the fall.

events.did: 确认自己从没爱过丈夫，丈夫也从未爱过她；婚礼几天后连那点友谊也死了
events.verbatim: Cynthia didn’t love her husband. Nor did Hubert ever love Cynthia. She had entertained the possibility of friendship during their brief courtship. But even that mild emotion died days after their wedding when his true nature emerged.

events.who: 辛西娅（对自己「如释重负」的定性）
events.did: 承认丈夫一死她有解脱感，但只是不必再假装婚姻完整快乐；她还想过天花、痛风、羞辱等轻恙，但「在书房地毯上流血而死」显然过头了
events.verbatim: If she did feel a breath of liberation at his demise, it was only because she no longer had to pretend her society marriage was whole and happy. Or that she was whole and happy, for that matter. … Which didn’t mean she wished ill upon Hubert. A mild malaise, perhaps. Boils on his willy for all his philandering. A burning case of gout. … But bleeding to death on the rug in his study seemed rather more than necessary. … ‘The man was prone to excess,’ Cynthia murmured. … ‘Probably the shock.’

events.did: 辛西娅主动问有没有嫌疑人、断言丈夫不是自然死亡；警司答的是「你会不会希望丈夫死」；辛西娅心里想「她能想出几百条理由」
events.verbatim: ‘Have you any suspects in Hubert’s murder?’ She feared she knew the superintendent’s answer. ‘It’s clear he didn’t die from natural causes.’ … ‘Lady Burrows, it gives me no pleasure to ask, but I must. Is there any reason you might want your husband dead?’ … Because she could think of hundreds of reasons.

events.did: 七月中午客厅里竟生着炉火，辛西娅推测是希金斯太太点的；往常这时客厅闷热，今天她却在发抖
events.verbatim: Mrs Higgins must have lit it, which was mad for mid-July. … Usually, the parlour was sweltering in the afternoon heat, but today she was shivering.
